property_summary: For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and deposit value, the reference contract ensures that Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (i.e., Put never sets a past unlockTime), whereas the mutant can set acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, breaking that invariant.

After any Put(...) call by any actor with any value, the reference contract always ensures Acc[actor].unlockTime >= block.timestamp, while the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can make Acc[actor].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For any caller, if Put is invoked with _unlockTime less than or equal to block.timestamp then the reference contract will set Acc[caller].unlockTime to block.timestamp (not less than block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, so we assert that Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put.

After Put is called by an address with zero prior balance, the reference sets Acc[actor].unlockTime to at least block.timestamp (monotone non-past for fresh accounts), whereas the mutant can set a freshly created account's unlockTime to a past timestamp when provided a past _unlockTime.

For every caller and any fuzzed _unlockTime and deposit, after calling Put the reference contract guarantees Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now), whereas the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating that invariant.

For any caller and any positive msg.value, after calling Put(...) the caller's Acc balance in the correct contract strictly increases by msg.value (i.e. new balance = old balance + msg.value); the mutant resets acc.balance to zero after adding, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any amount, calling Put(value) increases that caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly msg.value (new = old + value); the mutant overwrites acc.balance to 0 and thus violates this for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero ether value sent to Put, the contract's total stored balance for that caller (Acc[msg.sender].balance) is never less than the sum of all prior recorded balance and the just-sent msg.value (i.e., Put does not zero-out the stored balance after adding msg.value) — the mutant sets acc.balance to 0 after adding msg.value, violating this by making the post-Put recorded balance less than expected for some inputs.

For any caller and any sent ether amount, after calling Put the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is set to either the provided _unlockTime (if in the future) or block.timestamp, and this invariant holds for the reference but the mutant still sets unlockTime the same—so instead assert that the contract's balance mapping Acc[msg.sender].balance equals the contract's internal recorded balance observed via address(c).balance change: specifically, when a caller sends value v to Put, address(c).balance increases by v and simultaneously Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by at most that same v (i.e., the contract's on-chain ETH balance must reflect at least the recorded per-account increase); the mutant which zeroes acc.balance can make the per-account recorded balance not reflect the increase while address(c).balance still increases, so comparing address(c).balance delta vs Acc[msg.sender].balance delta detects the bug.

For any caller and any sent ether value, after calling Put(...) the contract's on-chain ETH balance increases by the sent amount and the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance increases by at least 1 (i.e., nonzero) when a positive value is sent; the mutant that sets acc.balance = 0 can make the recorded per-account balance remain zero while the contract's ETH balance increases, violating this rule for some inputs.

After calling Put by any actor with any value, the holder's recorded balance in C equals the contract's previous balance for that holder plus the sent value (i.e., Put always atomically increments Acc[actor].balance by msg.value); the mutant removing the reentrancy guard allows a reentrant attacker to reenter during Put and cause Acc[actor].balance to differ from the expected increment.

For any caller and amount, after Put(amount) returns the caller's Acc.balance equals the previous Acc.balance plus the sent amount (i.e., Put is effectfully atomic and increments balance by msg.value); removing the nonReentrant_ guard allows a reentrant attacker to disturb that invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and ether amount, a malicious reentrant callee cannot cause the caller's recorded Acc.balance to be less than the total ether that caller has ever sent to C (i.e., Acc[msg.sender].balance >= totalSent), but removing the nonReentrant_ guard allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during Put and make Acc.balance smaller than the total sent.

For any caller and amount sent to Put, Put must never revert (i.e., Put always returns/finishes successfully); removing the nonReentrant_ guard can allow a reentrant attacker (via fallback) to trigger a failing low-level external call during Put which can make Put revert for some inputs, so the buggy mutant can cause Put to fail while the reference never does.

For any caller and sent value, calling Put(x) on the reference contract never allows reentrant calls to Collect during the same Put invocation, so after Put returns the caller's Acc.balance is at least the value they just sent; removing the nonReentrant_ guard allows a reentrant attacker (via fallback) to call Collect during Put and cause Acc.balance to be reduced below the deposited amount for some inputs.
Collect never reverts when a caller with sufficient balance and expired unlockTime requests an allowed amount (i.e., successful send must not revert).

property_summary: If the caller's stored balance is at least MinSum, at least the requested amount, and the unlockTime has passed, then Collect should not revert (i.e., callers satisfying those conditions can successfully call Collect).
If Collect is called when the caller's stored balance is >= MinSum and >= requested amount and unlockTime has passed, then the call should not revert (reverted == false).

If the contract's account has at least MinSum and the caller's stored balance is at least the requested amount and the unlockTime has passed, then Collect either succeeds or (in P) does not revert due to failed external send — i.e. Collect does not revert when the call would fail silently.
If the caller's stored balance is strictly less than MinSum, Collect must revert (i.e., callers with balance < MinSum cannot successfully Collect).

Invariant: Collect never reverts for a recipient that rejects payments (the reference ignores failed low-level sends and continues, whereas the mutant reverts on failed send causing Collect to revert for some inputs).

For any caller and amount where the caller has sufficient balance and past unlockTime, Collect succeeds (does not revert) even if the recipient reverts during the low-level send; the mutant that requires the call to succeed will sometimes revert instead, breaking this rule.

For any caller, amount, and a recipient contract that intentionally reverts on receipt, the reference contract C allows Collect(...) to complete (it ignores failed low-level send) while the mutant that requires the send to succeed causes Collect(...) to revert when the recipient reverts; thus the reference never reverts in this adversarial scenario but the mutant does for some inputs.

For any caller with sufficient recorded balance and unlockTime passed, calling Collect(amount) never reverts even if the recipient address (msg.sender) rejects or reverts on receiving Ether; the mutant changes the call to require success, causing Collect to revert for some inputs when the recipient rejects payments.

For any caller with sufficient recorded balance (>= MinSum and >= requested amount) and whose unlockTime is in the past, Collect(amount) on the reference contract always completes (does not revert) even if the recipient rejects the incoming Ether; the mutant that requires the low-level send to succeed will revert for some such inputs when the recipient reverts.
After a successful Put followed by a successful Collect of the full deposited amount, the caller's recorded balance in c becomes zero (i.e., Collect reduces balance by transferred amount).

A single external call to Collect should never revert when called on its own (no nested reentry) if the caller had sufficient recorded balance and unlock time — i.e., under valid preconditions Collect succeeds.

If a call to Collect by any address reverts, then it must be because the caller did not have both sufficient recorded balance (>= _am and >= MinSum) and passed unlockTime, so with those preconditions Collect never reverts.

If the caller's recorded balance is at least MinSum and at least the requested amount _am and the unlockTime has passed, then Collect does not revert on the original contract (so reverted must be false).

When Collect is called by an address that has never called Collect in this transaction (i.e., no prior reentrant call from this test contract), then a single external call to Collect either succeeds or reverts only based on c's public conditions; specifically, if the call reverts then it must be because caller had insufficient recorded balance or unlockTime — equivalently, if the caller meets those public conditions the call does not revert (i.e., original contract does not permanently lock out future non-reentrant calls within different transactions).
